Synopsis:
Icelandic voters rejected restarting EU accession talks (52.8% against) in a referendum on 30 Aug 2026. Iceland's foreign minister acknowledged the unchanged geopolitical reality — shaped notably by Trump's posture on Greenland and NATO commitment — and signalled a pivot toward bilateral security agreements (Finland, Norway, Japan, Canada) and deeper EEA cooperation. Iceland remains outside the EU but inside the single market via the EEA. All Icelandic parties are now aligned behind EEA membership.
